Tell It Like It Is
TEL it lyk it IZ
phrase (Boomer slang)
African-American colloquial of the 1960s, meaning to speak frankly and truthfully without softening, popularized by the civil-rights movement and by Aaron Neville’s hit "Tell It Like It Is" (late 1966, No. 2 pop, No. 1 R&B). By 1968 it was a general expression of praise for blunt honesty, used by everyone from preachers to sportscasters (Howard Cosell made it his motto).

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To tell it like it is is to speak plainly and honestly, without spin or sugarcoating — and in the 1960s it was high praise, the opposite of the establishment’s smooth evasions. The Christian observation: Scripture loves plain truth-telling and gives it two partners the slogan sometimes forgets. First, truth itself: "Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another" (Eph 4:25). The prophets told it like it was to kings. Nathan stood before David, who had committed adultery and murder, and said, "Thou art the man" (2Sa 12:7). Paul asked the Galatians, "Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?" (Gal 4:16). "Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful" (Pro 27:6). Second, love: "speaking the truth in love" (Eph 4:15). Telling it like it is can become an excuse for cruelty — "I’m just being honest" — and Scripture does not bless honesty that wounds for the pleasure of wounding. Third, grace: "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man" (Col 4:6). Nathan told David the truth by telling him a story first, and he did it to bring him to repentance, not to win an argument. A father who tells his son the truth plainly, lovingly, and at the right time is telling it like it is in the biblical sense.

Webster 1828 Definition

1960s AAVE phrase (Aaron Neville hit, 1966) for speaking frankly without softening — a truth-telling Scripture commends (Eph 4:25; 2Sa 12:7) when it is joined to love (Eph 4:15) and grace (Col 4:6).

TELL IT LIKE IT IS, phr. (1960s; Boomer era) To speak frankly and honestly; to describe a situation truthfully without euphemism or evasion. "At least he tells it like it is."

Webster (1828) — TELL, verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive told. [Latin telum; Latin appello and peal, Latin pello.] 1. To utter; to express in words; to communicate to others. I will not eat till I have told my errand. Genesis 24:23 . 2. To relate; to narrate; to rehearse particulars; as, to tell a story. Genesis 37:16 . And not a man appears to tell their fate. 3. To teach; to inform; to make known; to show by words. tell us the way. Why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife? Gen 12.

Decode for families: "keeping it real" and "no filter" are its descendants. Ask whether love is in the room too.

Key Scripture

Eph 4:25 — "Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another."

Eph 4:15 — "But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ:"

2Sa 12:7 — "And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;"

Gal 4:16 — "Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?"

Pro 27:6 — "Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful."

Col 4:6 — "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man."

Modern Corruption

The phrase rightly praises plain truth over evasion but can excuse cruelty as honesty; Scripture demands truth spoken in love and seasoned with grace.

expand to see more

The 1960s were sick of euphemism — the government’s word games about Vietnam, the smooth lies of advertising, the silence of churches about segregation. Tell it like it is was a cry for honesty, and it was often a righteous one. Scripture has always demanded it; the prophets were the original truth-tellers, and they paid for it.

But a culture that prizes bluntness for its own sake slides toward brutality. "I’m just telling it like it is" becomes the excuse for every cruel word. Eph 4:15 holds the two together: truth and love are not rivals but partners. The truth without love is a club; love without truth is a lie. Nathan’s parable is the model — perfect honesty, delivered with wisdom, aimed at the sinner’s restoration.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English tellan (to count, to relate) → tell; 1960s AAVE tell it like it is → Aaron Neville, 1966 → general praise for frankness.
